QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_72

question.text: A Cat III AIF follows a long-short strategy. The MOST appropriate primary benchmark would be:

answer.text: A fixed absolute-return hurdle (e.g., 10% p.a.) set in the PPM

explanation.text: The Logic: Long-short funds target absolute returns with market-neutral or limited beta exposure — the right benchmark is a pre-determined absolute hurdle. The Trap: NIFTY 50 benchmarks long-only exposure; commodities/gold are unrelated to equity L/S. Cross-Exam Context: From Section 6.3 (absolute return strategies). Distributor's Pro-Tip: Educate investors that L/S fund performance shouldn't be judged by NIFTY alone — hurdle is the right yardstick.
